zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted on Deck 7 (a non-guest deck), directly beneath the Deck 8 Balcony/Oceanview cabins.
zones.effect: Looking straight down from a Deck 8 balcony you see boat canopy/tackle instead of water; the horizon and side view remain open and unobstructed.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who want to watch the water directly below or lean over the rail; does not matter to anyone focused on the horizon, sunbathing, or general balcony use.
zones.source: boards.cruisecritic.com (two independent threads confirm lifeboats sit on Deck 7 and block the straight-down view from Deck 8); cruisebooking.com lists Deck 8 as lifeboat-obstructed.

zones.what: Deck 8 Balcony/Oceanview cabins sit directly above the Escape Theater, Headliners comedy club and The Cavern Club, all housed in the Deck 6-7 entertainment complex.
zones.effect: Show music, bass, and rehearsal noise can carry up into these cabins, especially late evening and during matinee rehearsals; cruisedeckplans specifically flags the 'indented' balconies on this deck as sitting above the main theater.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and early-to-bed guests should avoid; nightlife-oriented guests who don't mind ambient bass won't notice much.
zones.source: cruisebooking.com (Deck 6-7 entertainment complex noise into Deck 8); cruisedeckplans.com Deck 8 page (indented balconies above main theater); boards.cruisecritic.com forum thread asking about Deck 8 cabins above the Escape Theater.

zones.what: Some Deck 9 mid-ship cabins sit directly above The District Brew House (craft-beer hall) on Deck 8, and are also close to the central elevator bank.
zones.effect: A guest holding cabin 9184 specifically raised concern about combined elevator-lobby traffic noise and brewhouse activity below; this is a real, ship-specific worry rather than a generic aggregator claim, though no confirmed outcome was posted.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests sensitive to bar/crowd noise and elevator-lobby traffic; not a concern for cabins elsewhere on Deck 9 away from the brewhouse footprint.
zones.source: boards.cruisecritic.com thread on cabin 9184, noting proximity to the elevator bank and to the District Brew House below.

zones.what: Balcony cabins in categories BA/BB/BC on Deck 14 sit directly beneath the pool deck and the Garden Café buffet.
zones.effect: Early-morning deck-chair dragging and pool-party noise from above can be heard in these cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who sleep in or are noise-sensitive in the early morning; less relevant to guests who are up and out early anyway.
zones.source: cruisebooking.com Norwegian Escape cabins-to-avoid guide, naming Deck 14 categories BA/BB/BC as being below the pool deck and Garden Café.

zones.what: Forward Penthouse cabins 14106 and 14706 have only a small side balcony that is enclosed within the steel hull and shaded by the bridge structure directly above (the bridge sits on Deck 15 on this ship).
zones.effect: The balcony feels boxed-in and shaded rather than open; sightlines to the side/down are cut off by steel plating, though this is a structural recess rather than a lifeboat obstruction.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests expecting a full open-air balcony in a Penthouse category; less relevant to guests who value the forward Penthouse's other perks (space, Haven access) over balcony openness.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Norwegian Escape Deck 14 page, naming cabins 14106/14706 specifically and matching this ship's known bridge position on Deck 15 (distinct wording from sister-ship pages, so not simple boilerplate).

zones.what: Forward balcony/spa-suite cabins on Deck 15 that sit close to the bridge have a large structural overhang from the deck above that shades part of the balcony.
zones.effect: A first-person review of a Spa Junior Suite balcony on this ship described a 'large steel canopy overhang above' the balcony; despite the overhang, the sea view itself stayed unobstructed by the glass balustrade.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to sun-seekers who want an uncovered balcony; doesn't matter to guests who value shade or an unobstructed horizon view.
zones.source: reasonstocruise.com first-person Norwegian Escape Spa Junior Suite review describing the steel canopy overhang and unspoilt view; corroborated generally by cruisedeckplans.com Deck 15 page noting an overhang shading balconies near the bridge.

zones.what: Forward-most cabins on Decks 14 through 16 are reported to carry the strongest motion in rough seas on this ship.
zones.effect: Guests prone to seasickness may feel more pitching/rolling in these high, forward cabins than midship or lower cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to motion-sensitive travelers; less relevant to guests sailing calm itineraries or those unaffected by ship movement.
zones.source: cruisebooking.com Norwegian Escape cabins-to-avoid guide identifying forward Decks 14-16 as the highest-motion cabins.

zones.what: Norwegian Escape has connecting cabins (e.g., in the 8100s range) whose adjoining doors are less soundproofed than a standard cabin wall.
zones.effect: Noise and conversation from the connected neighboring cabin can carry through more easily than through a normal wall.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests not traveling as a connected group who get assigned next to noisy connecting-door neighbors; not an issue for families who want the connecting feature.
zones.source: elliestraveltips.com Norwegian Escape cabins-to-avoid guide noting connecting-door sound transfer; corroborated by a ship-specific forum question about connecting cabin 8122.

zones.what: Norwegian Escape's wheelchair-accessible staterooms (Inside/Oceanview on Deck 5; Balcony-category accessible rooms scattered across Decks 9-15, e.g., 9924, 10286, 10886, 11918, 12282/12286, 12882, 12912, 13912, 14278/14282, 14878/14882, 14906, 15886) are positioned close to the ship's elevators.
zones.effect: Wider doors and roll-in showers come with the trade-off of being near elevator-lobby foot traffic and noise.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to mobility-need guests weighing accessibility convenience against elevator-lobby noise; not relevant to guests without accessibility requirements.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com Norwegian Escape cabins page, listing specific accessible cabin numbers and stating they are located close to the ship's elevators.

zones.what: The Studio (solo-traveler) staterooms occupy three consecutive decks (10, 11, 12) with a single-story Studio Lounge on Deck 11, a layout unique among this ship's sisters (Joy has no Studios at all).
zones.effect: Studio guests get a self-contained, keycard-only vertical enclave with its own lounge one deck away rather than spread across many separate zones.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to solo travelers deciding on Studio bookings; not relevant to other cabin types.
zones.source: thiscruiselife.com Breakaway vs Breakaway Plus comparison, describing Studio staterooms spanning Decks 10-12 with the Studio Lounge on Deck 11.

leads.claim: Guest asked whether this forward-most Deck 14 balcony is obstructed, suspecting it may be one of the balconies enclosed in metal on all sides.
Forward Penthouse cabins on Deck 13 have only a small side balcony (similar constrained-balcony pattern to 14106/14706 one deck up).
These Deck 8 balconies are partly angled, giving more space but sacrificing privacy since neighboring cabins can see onto the angled portion.
These Deck 8 balconies (100 sq ft) are partly overlooked from cabins on the deck above.
Guest worried this cabin's noise level would suffer from proximity to the elevator bank and from sitting above The District Brew House.
Guest asked about noise levels through the connecting door in this cabin; no confirmed answer found.

unknowns: No ship-specific confirmation found for I-95 crew-corridor access points or where they intersect guest cabin hallways on Norwegian Escape.
No ship-specific confirmation found for bow-thruster noise in far-forward Deck 5 cabins on Norwegian Escape (only generic claims for other NCL ships were found).
No ship-specific confirmation found for anchor-chain noise in forward cabins on Norwegian Escape (only generic claims for other ships/lines were found).

Aggregator claims describing 'aft cabins on lower Decks 5-6' with the most engine vibration do not match the real cabin inventory, since Deck 5 has no aft-section cabins and Deck 6 has no guest cabins at all; the true lowest aft-facing guest cabins are on Deck 9, and no source specifically confirms vibration levels there.

No evidence was found that this class has a true 'hump' (balconies cantilevered past the hull line); the only confirmed hull modification versus the Breakaway-class sisters is a uniform 5-foot hull widening that added about 40cm to all balcony widths, not a cantilevered hump on specific decks/sections.
Whether the Deck 8 lifeboat obstruction has any secondary, lesser effect on Deck 9 balconies immediately above was not confirmed by any source found this session.
Exact deck/location of the main pool deck relative to Deck 14 (used to support the 'below pool deck' noise claim) was not independently verified beyond a single aggregator source.
